eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models for Ankara on August 28 show a tight range around 26–27°C as the most likely daily maximum, with limited upside risk from instability.** 

Official guidance from the Turkish Meteorological Service and multiple global models (including ECMWF and GFS runs) indicate a high near 26–27°C (79–81°F), driven by northerly flow advecting cooler air and increasing cloud cover that reduces peak solar insolation. Afternoon convection and scattered thunderstorms—forecast with 30–50% probability in several updates—are expected to develop by midday or early afternoon, further capping temperatures through evaporative cooling and reduced sunshine. 

This follows hotter conditions on August 27 (highs near 32°C), with the shift tied to a passing trough and rising instability indices. Historical August climatology for Ankara averages highs around 30–31°C, so the current pattern represents a notable but not extreme departure. Model consensus remains close between 26°C and 27°C, with smaller probabilities for 28°C or higher only if storms hold off longer than anticipated or if boundary-layer mixing proves stronger than expected. Traders are weighting the latest hourly guidance and ensemble spreads, which show limited divergence on maximum temperature but greater uncertainty on exact timing of precipitation.

**Persistent cloud cover and widespread light rain are suppressing daytime heating in Beijing on August 28, 2026, anchoring the market-implied probability of a 24°C high at 87%.** Official forecasts from the China Meteorological Administration and international models (including ECMWF and GFS runs referenced in multiple services) converge on a maximum of 20–25°C under overcast skies with periods of drizzle or light rain, light northerly to westerly winds, and high humidity. These conditions limit incoming solar radiation and evaporative cooling effects, preventing temperatures from climbing toward the seasonal late-August average of ~30°C.

Recent developments reinforce this outlook: a frontal or monsoon-related system has brought cooler, unsettled weather across northern China since August 26–27, with Beijing recording highs near 24–28°C amid showers. Model consensus shows no significant warming trend or clearing until August 29, when drier, sunnier conditions are expected to push highs into the low 30s. Traders are weighting the strong agreement among short-range forecasts and the absence of any warm-air advection signals, keeping the 25°C+ outcomes at single-digit implied probabilities while the narrow 24°C band dominates.

eventMetadata.context_description: A warm, dry air mass is driving above-average highs for São Paulo on August 28, with official and ensemble forecasts from sources like Meteoblue, Climatempo, and IPMet converging on maxima of 31–33°C under sunny skies and negligible precipitation. This setup produces rapid daytime warming, low humidity near 30%, and light northwesterly winds, pushing readings well above the late-August climatological average of roughly 22–28°C. Model outputs vary modestly between 30°C and 33°C depending on boundary-layer mixing and exact steering, creating the observed market clustering around 31–33°C as traders weigh the most recent runs and historical analogs for similar synoptic patterns. Updated guidance issued August 27 reinforces this trajectory before a frontal passage brings cooler, wetter conditions early the following week.

Model consensus points to highs near 84–87 °F at key measurement sites, with small differences in timing of the marine layer or afternoon wind strength accounting for the near-even split between the 84–85 °F and 86–87 °F bins. eventMetadata.context_description: Recent multi-model forecasts from sources including ECMWF, GFS, and national meteorological services converge on a daytime high of 24–25 °C for Mexico City on 28 August, driven by the city’s 2,240 m elevation, widespread cloud cover, and frequent convective showers typical of the late-summer rainy season. These conditions suppress surface heating and limit afternoon maxima, consistent with climatological normals of roughly 23–25 °C. Model consensus and current observations of persistent moisture and light winds underpin the market’s heavy weighting toward 25 °C (51 % implied probability), with secondary support for 24 °C and 26 °C reflecting minor spread in guidance. No heat-wave signals or clearing trends have emerged in the latest runs.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models indicate a typical late-August rainy season pattern over Panama City, Panama, with morning temperatures climbing into the low 30s Celsius before widespread afternoon convection develops. High humidity and frequent thunderstorms—driven by the Intertropical Convergence Zone and local sea-breeze convergence—are expected to limit peak heating, keeping the daily maximum near 31–32 °C. Ensemble guidance shows only modest spread in timing and coverage of showers, creating the near-even split between those two outcomes in trader pricing. Official observations from the Panama meteorological service and surrounding stations will determine the precise highest reading for market resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest Met Office guidance and supporting numerical weather models show a maximum of 22 °C for London on 29 August under unsettled conditions with widespread showers and southwesterly flow. Persistent cloud cover and rainfall are expected to limit surface heating, keeping values near late-August climatological normals of 20–22 °C. Ensemble spreads and minor timing differences in shower bands create the close contest between 20 °C, 21 °C, and 22 °C outcomes, while stronger insolation or delayed rain would be required to push readings to 23 °C or higher. Updated model runs and the next Met Office briefing remain the key near-term catalysts for shifts in implied probabilities.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from European models and Météo-France indicate an Atlantic frontal system will deliver cooler maritime air to northern France, with southwest winds and variable cloud cover limiting daytime heating on August 29. Consensus points to a daily maximum near 22–23 °C, slightly below the 1991–2020 average high of 24.1 °C for the date, following a brief warm spell earlier in the week. Light showers or drizzle in some runs could further suppress temperatures, while clearer intervals support the upper end of the range. Traders have concentrated probability on 22–24 °C outcomes, reflecting this model agreement and limited upside potential absent a stronger ridge. Updated runs from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts and local observations over the next 48 hours will provide the final guidance ahead of market resolution.

Recent days featured hotter conditions (highs 31–36°C), but increasing moisture and cloud cover are expected to moderate temperatures.

**Key differentiating factors include precipitation timing and cloud cover, which limit peak solar heating and surface warming.** Thunderstorm development can cap the maximum 1–2°C below clear-sky potential through evaporative cooling and reduced insolation. Updated model runs and official briefings over the next 24–48 hours will provide the clearest resolution signals.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Approaching frontal system and associated cloud cover with light rain are the main drivers moderating Warsaw's peak temperature on August 29.** Multiple forecast models converge on daytime highs of 21–22°C under mostly overcast skies, with southerly winds and scattered showers limiting solar heating compared to the clearer, warmer conditions of 25–26°C expected on August 27–28. This reflects a shift from high pressure to a cooler, moister air mass, consistent with typical late-August patterns where precipitation reduces diurnal temperature range. Consensus places the highest likelihood near 21–22°C, though exact peak timing relative to rainfall introduces modest uncertainty in final observed maximum.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent official forecasts from Taiwan’s Central Weather Bureau and supporting models project a daytime high of 33–34 °C in Taipei on August 29, with partly cloudy skies and afternoon thunderstorms expected to limit peak heating. This outlook follows several days of stronger insolation that produced 35–36 °C readings earlier in the week, but increased cloud cover and moisture associated with a departing typhoon’s outer circulation are now suppressing temperatures. Afternoon convection typically peaks after 13:00 local time, aligning with the period when maximum readings are recorded. With only two days remaining, the next model runs and any revised CWB bulletins will be the key catalysts for shifts in trader-implied probabilities centered on the 34–35 °C range.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent cloud cover, showers, and moderate southwesterly winds are the main factors capping the daily maximum near 21–23 °C in Amsterdam on 29 August.** 

Forecasts from multiple sources, including GFS and ECMWF-derived guidance, show a high around 21–22 °C (roughly 70–71 °F) under mostly cloudy skies with periods of light rain or showers. These conditions limit solar heating compared with clearer days earlier in the week. Historical climatology places the average high for 29 August near 21 °C, so current model runs sit close to that baseline rather than producing a strong warm or cool anomaly.

The closely matched market prices (22 °C at 37 %, 23 °C at 31 %, 21 °C at 18.5 %) reflect genuine uncertainty in the precise peak, which depends on the exact timing and intensity of showers and small differences in boundary-layer mixing. Stronger or more persistent rain would favor the lower side of the range, while any break in cloud cover could allow a brief spike toward 23 °C. With the market resolving on official observations (typically Schiphol or a central Amsterdam station), traders are weighting the consensus forecast heavily while leaving room for last-minute model adjustments before the day.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

**Persistent southwest monsoon activity, reinforced by a nearby low-pressure area east of northern Luzon, is suppressing daytime heating in Metro Manila and anchoring forecast highs for August 29 near 28–29 °C.** 

Official PAGASA outlooks and multiple numerical models (including recent runs referenced in extended forecasts) show widespread cloud cover, scattered to widespread thunderstorms, and moderate-to-strong southwesterly winds that limit solar insolation and promote evaporative cooling. This keeps maximum temperatures from climbing toward 31 °C or higher while preventing significant cooling below 27 °C. Historical August climatology for Manila places average highs near 31 °C, but the active monsoon phase this week has already produced daily maxima in the 28–30 °C range, reinforcing trader confidence in the 28–30 °C band that now accounts for roughly 85 % of the market-implied probability. 

No rapid clearing or intensification signals appear in the latest guidance before the 29th, so near-term model consensus continues to favor the narrow 28–29 °C window as the most probable outcome.
